contracts: Client and route setup precede peer spawn. Clients remain alive while operation result and all relevant peer results are observed.
Returned single/paired completion futures own input raw handles before first poll. Paired failure branches observe both actual results or abort and join the pending sibling.

ControlledAcquisition owns tasks synchronously before its async preparation future can be polled. Preparation failures abort all tasks and preserve typed primary plus completed cleanup objects. Interrupted cleanup retains current and remaining lexical abort owners.
Contextual timeout wrappers preserve the original static operation messages and expose the original Elapsed through Error::source. Inner operation failures are not remapped.
TCP tests inspect all requested HTTPS-proxy purposes and CONNECT-UDP TCP connector settings; they do not claim native socket options or wire parity.
All unchanged route field/Close/auth/path and acquisition test literals were inspected in the complete candidate routing/owner source and full changed-line diff.
limits: No Cargo, runtime, network, or tracked modifications performed. Compilation and fixed native execution remain parent-owned.
Drop requests abort synchronously; it does not synchronously prove task destruction. Explicit stop is asynchronously bounded. Normal success joins depend on the existing outer fixture deadline.
FixtureFailures exposes primary through standard source and retains cleanup as a concrete field; all secondary causes are not promised as one linear source chain.
Supporting production/client ranges are partial. This does not close whole-file, whole-workspace, browser, or architecture coverage.
